title: GP-UCB vs epsilon-greedy for constrained budget-allocation levers
setting: Three segments share a budget through proportional allocation. Weights lie on a 0.1-step grid (271 arms after the anchor constraint that at least one weight is 1.0), and each weight may move by at most one step per round. The reward is a smooth, non-monotone function of the weights, observed with Gaussian noise and optional delay, over T=52 rounds. The environment is stationary, drifting (landscape parameters random-walk every 10 rounds) or reactive (an adversarial landscape blended in at 20% penalises the region near the agent's last action). The metric is cumulative regret against the per-round oracle best arm, computed from noise-free expected rewards on a freshly drawn landscape for each seed. Each method's exploration parameter (epsilon scale or beta scale) is tuned per condition on separate fixed seeds.

paper.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for Constraint Black Box Lever Optimization
paper.claim: GP-UCB with a Matern+Linear composite kernel attains lower cumulative regret than an epsilon-greedy baseline on sparse, noisy allocation problems, including under drifting and reactive environments.

metric.name: cum_regret
metric.description: Sum over 52 rounds of (best expected reward in that round minus expected reward of the chosen allocation). Lower is better. Typical values are a few units.

factors.name: method
factors.description: epsilon_greedy: decaying-epsilon policy with per-arm sample means. gp_ucb_matern_linear: GP-UCB with a Matern(nu=1.5)+Linear kernel (the paper's method). gp_ucb_rbf: GP-UCB with an RBF-only kernel (ablation). All three move toward their chosen target under the step limit, and all have their exploration scale tuned on separate seeds.

factors.name: environment
factors.description: Reward-landscape dynamics: fixed, random-walk drift of landscape parameters every 10 rounds, or an adversarial blend that reacts to the agent's last action.

factors.name: noise_sd
factors.description: Standard deviation of Gaussian observation noise on the aggregate reward (reward values lie in roughly [0.2, 1]).

factors.name: delay
factors.description: Number of rounds by which feedback is delayed before the policy can use it.
